Question: Suppose you want to make cheese with as little lactose as possible. How would you do it?
Answer: There are at least two thousand types of cheese, and all have different personalities. Let us have a look at the processing of cheese in general. Take an example from Cheddar Cheese: It is not a washed curd cheese. Lactose is water soluble, and when the cheese is made, it is a liquid portion, which is technically called whey. Now, let us explain and do some calculations. We get about one kg of cheese out of 10 Kg of milk (It depends on the variety of cheese; some get more, and some get less). This figure is for an explanation. For example, we make cheddar cheese: We get one Kg of cheese from 10 kg of milk. During this process, we eliminated 90 percent of lactose (1 Kg of cheese and 9 kg of whey). This cheese was made from cow’s milk, and let us take a whole number: 5 percent was lactose. Therefore, we removed 450 g of lactose from 500 g of lactose in cheese. Now let me give you an example of washed curd cheeses, Such as Gouda/Edam/Harvarti, to name a few. In these cheeses, the curd is washed with hot water to eliminate lactose and make it mild, reducing the lactose content. Further aging/maturing reduces the lactose content of these cheeses. Conclusion: Depending on the variety of cheese, A good number or, say, a large number of cheeses only have a trace amount of low level of lactose. However: Here is a word of caution: Fresh and soft cheeses, due to their higher water/whey content and non-aging, have higher levels of lactose than the aged Cheddar, Gouda, Edam, and Harvarti categories. Cheese made from lactose-free milk/cream: For example, cream cheese made from lactose-free milk and cream is now available in some stores in Canada. Question: What are the requirements for Canadian citizens to migrate to the US? Is it possible for someone without a job in the US to immigrate? If so, what is the process?
Answer: It is so ironic most people in the rest of the world believe: Oh, Canada is next door; once we are in Canada, even with hocus pocus (fraudulent/illegal entry), we can walk across the bridge and get into the USA. And In the same way, people in the USA believe Canada is just snow and igloos. Stories go around that sometimes Americans show up in Toronto in the summer to Ski. Sometimes, ignorance is bliss; most of the time, ignorance is dangerous. Both countries have very cordial relations. This is not now due to the present government's total uselessness, but in the past, yes, we had good leaders. A Canadian can move to the USA with a job offer; it is called a TN Visa. If the job ends, so does the Visa. And, of course, when it comes to the Green Card, a Canadian who is not naturalized but born Canadian will be in line with Canadians. Indian or other nationalities but naturalized Canadian will be a line from the country of their origins. Of course, other avenues exist to gain legal entry, such as family reunions and marriage to American citizens. And there may also be some legitimate business visas available. Telling a lie and trying to outsmart the USA system will ban you for life, for sure. Getting legal papers to move to the USA without job offers is NOT a walk in the park, as most people believe. I know a few people who went to the USA on TN visas, but when their jobs were over and they could not get another one, they had to return to Canada. The USA has become very tough on visas to the USA. Even day trips across the border used to be going next door, but NOT anymore; you must have proper credentials to go for a day of cross-border shopping. I have seen at the borders that cars are all ripped apart if they get suspicious of anything. And NEVER, NEVER try to be funny or rude to them. You may spend much more time at the border than expected. Answer all the questions with politeness, truth, and facts. I have crossed the borders 100 s of times; I have a NEXUS card. I hope it helps Sam Arora: MSc Food Science U of Guelph, Canada MSc Dairy Science U of Punjab, NDRI, India
